findings.claim: The rear close is argued partly from the chapter division, a tier-4 fact, alongside the tier-1 onset that actually carries the seam.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'It closes on “those who grumble will receive instruction.” (web:Isa.29.24), the chapter’s closing verse, before the next hoy onset opens Isa.30.1', and literature_type_guess reads 'short promise oracle to the house of Jacob closing the chapter'; chapter and verse divisions are tier-4 metadata and are never boundary evidence. The ground that does stand is the verse-initial hoy of the next unit, ה֣וֹי בָּנִ֤ים סֽוֹרְרִים֙ (oshb:Isa.30.1, byte tier), one of exactly 6 verse-initial hoy verses in chs 28-33 (sweep: 6 verses — MT 28:1, 29:1, 29:15, 30:1, 31:1, 33:1). No parashah seg stands at MT 29:24 (the chapter's segs are SAMEKH at MT 29:8, 29:12, 29:14, 29:21), so absence there is not counterevidence and the rear seam rests on the next unit's onset alone. All other checks on this row pass: the opening splice collates at byte tier at oshb:Isa.29.22, both curly-quoted WEB runs are byte-verbatim at web:Isa.29.22 and web:Isa.29.24, the front-seam SAMEKH at MT 29:21 is correctly typed and disclosed single-witness, and the row's 'clean interior' claim is true (no seg, paseq or K/Q note falls in MT 29:22-29:24).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): drop 'the chapter’s closing verse' from boundary_rationale and 'closing the chapter' from literature_type_guess, leaving the hoy-onset ground to carry the rear seam.

findings.claim: The curly-quoted WEB gloss covers three words of a seven-word Hebrew splice, and the one construal-bearing word is glossed by a WEB clause that renders it 'concerning', not as an address.
findings.grounds: The splice is לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.29.22, byte tier, re-collated), seven words; the gloss offered for it is “the house of Jacob” (web:Isa.29.22), three words. WEB Isa.29.22's own clause reads 'Therefore Yahweh, who redeemed Abraham, says concerning the house of Jacob', so the second witness renders the preposition as 'concerning' while the row asserts 'an explicit divine-speech frame with a named addressee' and carries oracle_frame.addressee_shift at confidence high. No morphology layer is staged, so such a reading has to be argued from the pointed bytes plus BOTH witnesses' renderings; only one is engaged. The koh-amar frame itself is correctly attributed — the divine name stands inside the spliced formula — so the tier-1 onset is unaffected.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): extend the gloss to the splice extent and disclose the 'to'/'concerning' construal, or drop 'a named addressee' from the frame claim and keep the frame as the driver.

findings.claim: The digit cited for 'the book's other massa-headed oracles' is the full verse-initial massa inventory, which includes this row's own header, so the 'other' set is 9, not 10.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'the same verse-initial formal marker used to open the book’s other massa-headed oracles (sweep: 10 massa headers)'. A verse-initial sweep of the header word returns exactly 10 MT verses — 13:1, 15:1, 17:1, 19:1, 21:1, 21:11, 21:13, 22:1, 23:1, 30:6 — and the tenth is this row's own onset מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב (oshb:Isa.30.6, byte tier, re-collated). The header role is correctly split from the burden-noun sites, and the cut on it is a genuine tier-1 verse-initial marker.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): cite '(sweep: 10 verse-initial massa headers, this site among them)' or restate the comparator set as 9.

findings.claim: device_notes carries review-workflow language in row prose.
findings.grounds: device_notes reads 'the row argues the cut from the header’s own bytes rather than from the surrounding woe theme, and flags the tension for review'. The register purge bars workflow and administrative language in every row field; the exposure is already carried by the medium_low band and the frontier flag. The substantive disclosure around it is sound: the rival is byte-grounded (the closing clause of MT 30:6 against the clause MT 30:5 turns on, meeting at consonantal-skeleton tier and attested at exactly 2 verses book-wide — re-swept: skeleton hits MT 30:5 and MT 30:6 only, with byte and accent-stripped tiers separating them), and MT 30:5's K/Q note does sit earlier in that verse than the quoted clause.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): replace the clause with a substantive uncertainty statement about the header-versus-theme tension.

findings.claim: The row names a byte-true cross-seam continuity fact as 'the seam's real warrant' for its own front cut, and no tier-1 onset class stands in its opening verse's bytes.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads '...but the second-person plural ADDRESSEE carries across the seam: Isa.30.18’s object suffixes answer the same second-person plural running through Isa.30.15 and Isa.30.17. That addressee continuity, not a continuing speaking voice, is the seam’s real warrant.' The cited tokens are byte-true — גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם and אֲבִיתֶֽם (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier), תָּנֻ֑סוּ and נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם (oshb:Isa.30.17, byte tier) — and the answering suffix stands inside the row's own opener וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier). A byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity AGAINST the cut; disclosing it is right, but it cannot be the cut's warrant. What the opening verse's own bytes carry is a consequence connector, a backward-linking particle, not a hoy, massa, divine frame, addressee shift, vocative or imperative onset; the row itself states the addressee does not shift. The tier-3 layer also does not sit at this seam: MT 30:17 carries no seg (chapter 30's segs are SAMEKH at MT 30:5, 30:11, 30:18, 30:26, 30:33 and PE at MT 30:14), so the nearest marked division, at MT 30:18, falls AFTER the row's own opening verse, interior to the span. No frame-onset deviation is registered and frontier_flag_considered is false, at confidence medium.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): restate the addressee continuity as the disclosed cross-seam cohesion it is, name the ground the onset verse's own bytes carry, and register the frame-onset deviation or lower the band. Disagreement with the row's stated grounds — routed onward, not adjudicated here.

findings.claim: The 25-verse digit belongs to the substring class that blends bare and waw-prefixed forms, not to 'the bare particle' the prose names; the bare particle stands at 23 verses, and the row's own onset is the waw-prefixed form.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'the bare particle stands at exactly 25 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier and is the same connector, לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier), that opens the indictment frame earlier in this chapter'. Re-swept: the contiguous skeleton substring returns exactly 25 MT verses, but a word-bound token split of the same hit set gives 23 verses carrying the bare form and 2 carrying the waw-prefixed form — MT 8:7 and MT 30:18, the row's own opening verse. The row's onset is וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier), waw-prefixed, while its comparator לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier) is bare; the prefix difference is never disclosed, so a digit for one object is attached to prose naming another.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): either cite 23 verses for the bare particle and disclose that this row's own onset is the waw-prefixed form, or keep 25 and name the swept object as the skeleton class including waw-prefixed forms.

findings.claim: One boundary_evidence_refs array cites the same MT-keyed single-witness apparatus under two different witness prefixes.
findings.grounds: The refs carry 'oshb:Isa.30.25 (paseq, single-witness)' beside 'web:Isa.30.18 (setumah, single-witness)' and 'web:Isa.30.26 (setumah, single-witness)'; the parashah and paseq inventories are both MT-keyed and single-witness. The underlying facts all check out against the inventory: SAMEKH at MT 30:18 and MT 30:26, paseq at MT 30:25, the count-only convention respected ('tallying presence rather than placement'), and the next paseq site after MT 30:25 is indeed MT 31:4 — the ordered paseq run across chs 29-32 is exactly MT 30:25 then MT 31:4. No K/Q note falls inside MT 30:18-30:26, so none was owed.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): cite all three apparatus refs under oshb: keys.

findings.claim: The row cites one and the same parashah seg under two different witness prefixes in two of its fields.
findings.grounds: device_notes reads 'the existing SAMEKH mark at oshb:Isa.30.33 corroborating at tier-3', while boundary_evidence_refs carries 'web:Isa.30.33 (setumah, single-witness)'; the parashah layer is MT-keyed and single-witness, so one seg is being attributed to two witnesses. The seg itself is real and correctly typed, and it does close the row's rear seam. Everything else in this row's mark, variant and digit discipline re-verifies: SAMEKH at MT 30:26 at the front seam and SAMEKH at MT 30:33 at the close, no other seg and no paseq inside MT 30:27-30:33, K/Q notes at MT 30:32 and MT 30:33 both disclosed with the quoted closing clause sitting after MT 30:33's varying token, and the rear-edge catchword stem re-swept to exactly 2 verses book-wide (MT 30:33 and MT 31:6). All five Hebrew splices collate at byte tier at their cited refs and both curly-quoted WEB runs are byte-verbatim.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): cite the seg as oshb:Isa.30.33 in both fields.

findings.claim: The 18-verse digit for the verse-initial presentative names no tier, holds only at skeleton tier, and its eighteenth member there is a ketiv token rather than the pointed presentative the row names; the pointed form stands verse-initial at 17.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'The presentative הֵ֥ן opening this verse stands verse-initial at exactly 18 verses book-wide, only two of them in chapters 28-35'. Re-swept on first-token identity: 18 MT verses at consonantal-skeleton tier, 17 at accent-stripped tier. The skeleton-only member is MT 54:16, whose verse-initial token is the unpointed ketiv standing before its pointed qere; that verse is K/Q-bearing in the inventory, which is exactly the class the K/Q-before-counting rule guards. The row's own splice is the pointed form הֵ֥ן (oshb:Isa.32.1, byte tier, re-collated). The dependent sub-claim survives: at both tiers the only chs 28-35 members are MT 32:1 and MT 33:7.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): cite 17 verses at accent-stripped tier for the pointed presentative, or keep 18 while naming the skeleton tier and disclosing the MT 54:16 ketiv member.

findings.claim: device_notes lists a parashah mark as one of the three grounds the boundary rests on; in the Prophets the layer is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver.
findings.grounds: device_notes reads 'resting the boundary on the fresh subject (the coming king), the verse-initial presentative, and the parashah PE mark at oshb:Isa.32.8.' The mark is real and correctly typed — PE at MT 32:8, not conflated with the SAMEKH segs at MT 31:9 and MT 32:20 — and it is disclosed single-witness, but 'resting the boundary on' it makes a tier-3 signal load-bearing. The row's boundary_rationale keeps the same mark to the corroboration side ('corroborating the break'), so the two fields do not describe the mark's weight the same way.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): restate the PE as tier-3 corroboration of the rear seam and remove it from the list of grounds the boundary rests on.

findings.claim: Confidence high rests on grounds the row itself concedes are non-discriminating, while the stronger in-witness ground at the front edge is only alluded to.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale concedes 'the particle alone does not discriminate the two' and falls back on 'the topic itself, a coming king unconnected to anything preceding it'; device_notes' third ground is the tier-3 PE. The stronger available ground is the preceding unit's own tier-1 close, the postpositive signature נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.31.9, byte tier), which the row touches only as 'the closing signature'. frontier_flag_considered is false although the row registers a frame-onset deviation, where its sibling non-frame-onset rows in this stretch carry the flag.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): argue the front edge from the postpositive signature closing at oshb:Isa.31.9 and the SAMEKH there, or lower the band.

findings.claim: A curly-quoted WEB run is bound to an oshb: ref, and the verse it argues appears in the refs array only under a web: key.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'immediately before the vocative onset that opens the following unit at oshb:Isa.32.9, “Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice!”'. The run is byte-verbatim in WEB Isa.32.9, but it is English WEB text cited against the MT witness, and boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.32.9 with no oshb:Isa.32.9 to mirror the oshb: citation in the prose. The K/Q disclosure for this row is complete and correct: MT 32:7 carries a note and is disclosed, MT 32:15's note falls outside the span, and no seg other than the PE at MT 32:8 touches MT 32:1-32:8.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): cite the English run as web:Isa.32.9.

findings.claim: The row declines an interior seam at MT 33:13 on a stated rule that counts only hoy, massa and divine-frame markers, omitting the imperative-onset and addressee-shift class the tier-1 catalogue carries; its paired mark claim is byte-false at that very site, and the rule as stated is incompatible with the neighbouring unit's own onset.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale quotes the verse-initial summons שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.13, byte tier, re-collated), an imperative with named addressees, and its two digits re-verify exactly — verse-initial at 10 MT verses book-wide (MT 1:2, 1:10, 33:13, 46:3, 46:12, 48:1, 49:1, 51:1, 51:7, 66:5) and at this single site across chs 28-35. It then declines the site because 'none carries a fresh hoy, massa, or divine-frame marker of its own; it is that absence ... that keeps the complex bounded as one unit'. Two things cut against that. First, the row's next sentence says the SAMEKH segs at MT 33:6 and MT 33:12 mark 'internal stanza turns that bind to no fresh hoy or vocative marker of their own'; that is true at MT 33:6, whose following verse opens on the presentative הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, byte tier), but false at MT 33:12, whose division falls immediately before the summons the row itself quotes — so the tier-3 layer's own division does bind to a fresh vocative-imperative marker there. Second, the row names MT 33:13's summons as 'the same formal class as the summons opening web:Isa.34.1'; that onset, קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, byte tier), likewise carries no hoy, no massa and no divine frame, so the rule as stated would hold chapter 34 inside this unit as well, and the neighbouring row cuts there. On the rule the row states, its own rear seam at MT 33:24 is left without a positive warrant.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY, adjudication routed onward: either respan Isa.33.1-Isa.33.24 as Isa.33.1-Isa.33.12 plus Isa.33.13-Isa.33.24, cutting at the verse-initial summons with the SAMEKH at MT 33:12 as tier-3 corroboration; or hold the span and re-argue the decline on a ground that survives the tier-1 imperative-onset and addressee-shift class and that also distinguishes MT 33:13 from the neighbouring onset at MT 34:1.

findings.claim: The SAMEKH at MT 33:1 is presented as marking the unit's onset, but on the convention this corpus itself uses a seg at a verse closes the section after that verse, so this one divides MT 33:1 from MT 33:2 — interior to the row — and it is excluded from the row's own interior tally.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'This same onset, oshb:Isa.33.1, is itself marked by a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness)', and then 'Two further SAMEKH marks (single-witness), interior to the unit, fall at oshb:Isa.33.6 and oshb:Isa.33.12'. The inventory carries SAMEKH at MT 33:1, 33:6 and 33:12 — three segs, all inside MT 33:1-33:24 — plus the SAMEKH at MT 32:20 that the row correctly cites at its front seam, and a paseq at MT 33:14 correctly tallied count-only. Four sibling rows in this stretch read the layer the other way: the seg at MT 31:9 is 'the verse immediately ahead of this unit's own onset ... closed by a parashah SAMEKH', the seg at MT 32:8 'closes ... immediately before this unit's onset', the seg at MT 29:21 is the front-seam mark of a unit opening at MT 29:22, and the seg at MT 30:5 is the rear-seam mark of a unit closing at MT 30:5. Under that reading MT 33:1's seg cannot corroborate this unit's onset. Otherwise the span-relevant mark sweep is complete: no seg, paseq or K/Q note inside MT 33:1-33:24 is undisclosed, and MT 33:24 carries none.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): move MT 33:1 into the interior tally and let the front seam rest on the hoy onset with the SAMEKH at MT 32:20 as its tier-3 corroboration.

findings.claim: The curly-quoted WEB run for the onset verse is not byte-verbatim; it matches only after English normalisation.
findings.grounds: The run quoted for web:Isa.33.1 carries a straight apostrophe (U+0027) in 'weren't' where WEB Isa.33.1 reads 'weren’t' with the curly apostrophe (U+2019); every other character agrees. Re-checked across all eight rows in this slice, it is the only curly-quoted WEB run that fails a byte-verbatim check — the other thirteen are verbatim at their cited refs.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): re-splice the run from the WEB text rather than re-keying it.

findings.claim: device_notes closes on campaign-calibration narration rather than substrate description.
findings.grounds: device_notes reads 'The confidence recorded here, medium_low, sits at the campaign’s own ceiling for a whole-chapter span -- chapter 33 runs the full 24 verses -- and stays there because the cap is a calibration rule, not a signal that a fresh defect was found in the argument above.' The register purge bars workflow and administrative language in row prose. The cap itself is correctly applied: chapter 33 runs 24 verses in both witnesses and the row claims all 24, so medium_low is the right band.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): state the whole-chapter extent as the substrate fact it is and drop the calibration commentary.

findings.claim: The postpositive-signature key names a closure device that does not stand in the row's own closing verse and that the row explicitly declines as a frame.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals carries speech_formula.postpositive_signature, but the signature it names, עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.33.10, byte tier), stands mid-span, and boundary_rationale itself says it 'identifies the speaker within the continuing complex rather than opening a narrative or messenger-formula frame of its own'. The row's own closing verse carries no signature: MT 33:24 closes on נְשֻׂ֥א עָוֺֽן (byte tier). The row's other two keys, woe_series.onset and oracle_frame.scene_shift, do answer to devices in its own bytes.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): drop the closure key, or replace it with a key naming the interior speaker-identification signal it actually describes.
